boundaries: Keep required instructions visible. Use Tabs when each section represents a separate view.
recommendations: Use short section titles that explain the hidden content. Choose multiple expansion when users compare sections.

boundaries: Use Task List for progress through planned work. The application supplies and orders events.
recommendations: Use a consistent chronological order. Include the actor, action, and a meaningful timestamp.

boundaries: The application owns the reasoning stream and decides which steps to name. Agent Thinking shows them; it does not run tools or fetch sources.
Show reasoning the model chose to expose. Some providers only return a summary, or nothing.
recommendations: Pass the reasoning so far with status streaming, name the current step in stage, and set status to complete when the answer starts. Pass duration when showing a reply from history.

boundaries: Use Alert Dialog when a decision must interrupt the task. Do not announce routine updates as urgent alerts.
recommendations: Explain the status and a useful next action. Choose announcement urgency to match the message.

boundaries: Reserve interruption for consequential decisions. Use Dialog for ordinary editing tasks.
recommendations: State the consequence before the confirming action. Name both the action and the safe way to cancel.

boundaries: Up to six series. Fold the rest into "Other" or split into small multiples; never generate a seventh hue.
Use stacked or percent only when the series add up to a meaningful whole. Compare unrelated measures in separate charts, never on two y-axes.
recommendations: Put the largest, steadiest series first so it forms the base of the stack. Keep series order and tones fixed when filters change.

boundaries: The application runs the action and stores the decision. Approval Card only reports Approve, Deny, the note, and Always allow.
Use it for actions that are hard to undo, such as sending, deleting, or paying. For a tool call already on screen, Tool Call asks inline.
recommendations: Name the action in the title as a verb phrase, say why in the description, and list what will happen in details. Pass a denial's note to the agent so it can change course.

boundaries: Aspect Ratio controls geometry. Image descriptions, loading, and media playback belong to the child content.
recommendations: Reserve the intended media proportion before loading. Choose image fitting that preserves meaningful content.

boundaries: Use File Upload for file selection and upload progress. Attachment does not own transport or storage.
recommendations: Show the filename and useful metadata such as format or size. Label preview and download actions.

boundaries: Use Thumbnail for general media. An avatar should not be the only visible identifier for a person.
recommendations: Provide recognizable fallback content and useful image descriptions. Keep sizes consistent within the same context.

boundaries: The caller supplies members and overflow content. Use a list when users need to identify every participant.
recommendations: Give the group a shared name and keep ordering meaningful. Explain any omitted members nearby.

boundaries: Use Button or Link for explicit actions. A badge must not be the only indication of a critical state.
recommendations: Use short labels for status or category. Pair semantic color with text that carries the meaning.

boundaries: Use for nominal categories ranked by one measure. Rows always sort largest first; use CategoryComparison when the order is meaningful or values can be negative.
recommendations: Keep labels short so they stay on the bar. Show at most about ten rows and fold the rest into "Other".

boundaries: Use ordinary text for emphasis or summaries. Blockquote represents another source's words.
recommendations: Keep the quotation intact and put attribution outside the quoted text.

boundaries: Breadcrumbs describe hierarchy, not browser history. Do not make the current page a redundant navigation action.
recommendations: Show meaningful ancestors and name the current resource. Use real destinations for ancestor links.
Place decorative icons beside text as children. Give icon-only links and collapsed Menu triggers an accessible name.

boundaries: Use a link for navigation, including when composing with render.
Use Toggle for a persistent pressed state.
Use Alert Dialog when a destructive action needs confirmation.
recommendations: Use default or brand for the main action. Keep supporting actions quieter.
Give icon buttons an aria-label. Hide decorative icons from assistive technology.
Keep the label when loading. Loading blocks activation and preserves keyboard focus.
Tab moves focus. Enter or Space activates an enabled button.
Button supports Server Components. Add event handlers in a Client Component.

boundaries: Use Toolbar for arrow-key command navigation. Button Group preserves each button's native Tab behavior.
ButtonGroup does not provide toolbar arrow-key navigation.
recommendations: Connect buttons that act on the same task. Give the group an accessible name.

boundaries: Use Date Picker for compact editable entry. Date availability and booking rules belong to the application.
recommendations: Specify locale and unavailable dates. Use range mode when the task selects a stay or reporting interval.
Use minValue, maxValue, or isDateUnavailable for real date constraints.

boundaries: Dates are calendar days, not instants; convert timestamps to dates in the user's time zone first.
recommendations: Show up to a year. The grid scrolls sideways in narrow containers rather than shrinking days below a readable size.

boundaries: Spacing can group ordinary content without another card. Keep independent actions outside a card-wide link.
recommendations: Use a card for one meaningful resource or task. Keep its title, content, and actions in a clear reading order.

boundaries: Do not hide required instructions in later slides. Use a static list for content that users must compare together.
recommendations: Keep navigation controls labeled and slide ordering meaningful. Allow users to review content at their own pace.

boundaries: Use Time Series for change over time. Do not compare values measured in incompatible units.
recommendations: Order categories deliberately and keep the zero baseline visible. Explain the units and meaning of negative values.

boundaries: The chart definition owns the plot. Aggregation, filtering, and a readable data alternative belong to the application.
recommendations: Name the chart's question and provide readable units. Keep detailed values available beyond pointer hover.

boundaries: This legend is static. Do not imply filtering or toggling unless the application provides those controls.
The legend describes series; it does not toggle their visibility.
recommendations: Match series names and colors to the plot. Keep legend ordering consistent across related charts.

boundaries: The chart engine owns positioning and interaction. Essential information also needs a persistent readable representation.
ChartTooltip renders content; ChartFrame owns chart pointer and keyboard behavior.
recommendations: Show the selected observation's label, units, and exact values. Keep series names consistent with the legend.

boundaries: Use Radio Group for mutually exclusive choices. Use Switch for a setting that takes effect immediately.
recommendations: Use a visible label for each independent choice. Put explanations beside the option they describe.

boundaries: The group coordinates selected values. The application decides how those values affect records or permissions.
recommendations: Give the group a shared label and each option a distinct value. Use parent selection for an explicit select-all task.
Set allValues when using the parent checkbox so it can derive mixed state.

boundaries: Citation marks a work title. Use Link when the reader needs to open the source.
recommendations: Use the work's title and include enough surrounding context to identify the source.

boundaries: Use Code Block for multiline examples. Inline code should not substitute for a control or heading.
recommendations: Use inline code for identifiers, commands, and literal values within ordinary text.

boundaries: Code Block presents text and an optional copy action. It does not execute code or provide syntax highlighting.
recommendations: Name the file or language and include the imports needed to use the example. Copy the same text that is displayed.

boundaries: Use Accordion for related disclosure sections. Do not hide required input or critical errors.
recommendations: Name the content being revealed and keep the trigger visible after expansion.

boundaries: Use Select for a short fixed list. Remote search, request cancellation, and result loading belong to the application.
recommendations: Use filtering when the option set is hard to scan. Keep option labels distinct and explain empty results.

boundaries: Keep important actions available outside the palette. Use Combobox when selecting a form value.
recommendations: Use action names that describe outcomes. Group related commands and show shortcuts when they exist.

boundaries: Composer owns draft editing and input controls. Use Conversation for message history and auto-scroll, and Message for individual messages.
The caller owns sending, attachments, and retries. Submitting a draft does not prove successful delivery.
recommendations: Name the message input and submit action. Preserve the draft when sending fails.

boundaries: Provide a visible alternative for essential actions. Context menus must not be the only way to complete a task.
recommendations: Offer actions specific to the resource under the pointer. Match labels to the same actions elsewhere.

boundaries: Use Table for static records that do not need managed state.
Keep remote queries and destructive mutations in the application.
Sorting needs a configured TanStack sorting feature and row model.
recommendations: Keep search and filters near the records they affect.
State whether bulk selection covers a page or all filtered matches.
Keep data, columns, and feature configuration stable between renders.
Mark the identifying column as a row header so it freezes while the grid scrolls sideways.
Enable column resizing for wide working tables so people can fit columns to their data.

boundaries: Values are dates, not timestamps. Use Date Time Input when the task requires a local time as well.
recommendations: Label the date's purpose and state its constraints. Keep editable input and calendar selection available.

boundaries: Define endpoint and timezone meaning in the application. Presets do not replace server validation.
A first calendar click may be a pending start; a complete range has both endpoints.
recommendations: Explain the range's meaning and any stay limits. Use presets only for intervals relevant to the task.

boundaries: The control does not perform timezone conversion. The application resolves ambiguous or nonexistent local times.
recommendations: Show the intended timezone beside local date and time entry. Preserve the user's entered value on validation failure.

boundaries: Read-only structural diagrams. Use Charts for measurements and Task List for execution progress.
Install the optional pele peer and import Diagram from @mizen-labs/ui/diagram. Other Mizen entry points do not load the renderer.
Only flowchart, sequence, entity relationship, and state syntax are supported. Links, external images, custom icon markup, and math renderers are disabled.
recommendations: Provide a concise aria-label and an aria-description explaining the relationships, branches, or transitions.
Keep diagrams focused. Wide diagrams scroll locally rather than shrinking labels below the reading size.
Use default diagram colors so nodes follow the active theme. Source style directives can override them.

boundaries: Use Alert Dialog for critical confirmation. Move long, multi-step work to a page when the overlay obscures context.
recommendations: Give the task a clear title. Keep the main action and cancel action visible and predictable.
DialogTitle names the popup. DialogDescription supplies supporting context. Tab stays within a modal dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus to its trigger.
An uncontrolled composition can live in a Server Component. Use a Client Component for open state and callbacks. Close after a save succeeds, not before.

boundaries: The component counts supplied observations. Sampling, weighting, and statistical interpretation belong to the application.
recommendations: Set an explicit domain and a useful bin count. Describe the observations and show interval meaning.

boundaries: Dragging must not be the only dismissal path. Use a page for tasks that require sustained reference to other content.
recommendations: Use a clear title and an explicit close control. Keep scrolling content separate from the main action.

boundaries: Use Error State for failed loading. Empty content must not imply that a failed request returned no records.
recommendations: Explain whether data is absent or filtered out. Offer a relevant first action or a way to clear filters.

boundaries: Use Field Error for one invalid input and Empty for successful zero-result queries.
recommendations: Explain the failed operation and provide a realistic recovery action. Preserve usable content and entered values.

boundaries: Field connects accessible descriptions. Business rules and server validation remain application responsibilities.
recommendations: Compose the label, control, description, and error together. Explain how to correct an invalid value.
Clicking FieldLabel focuses its control. FieldDescription and visible FieldError text describe that control to assistive technology.
Static composition can live in a Server Component. Validation functions, bound form state, and event handlers belong in a Client Component.

boundaries: Use Field for one control. A visual panel alone does not establish a form group.
recommendations: Use a legend that describes the shared question. Keep individual control labels inside the group.

boundaries: The application owns transport, cancellation, and retries. Validate file content and limits on the server.
recommendations: Show accepted formats and size limits before selection. Keep rejection reasons and progress beside each file.

boundaries: Form coordinates client validation and submission. The server must validate submitted data and authorize mutations.
The focused example validates local form state. It does not persist data.
recommendations: Show field errors near their controls. Preserve values after failed submission and provide a clear retry action.

boundaries: Use Frame for a meaningful work area. Avoid wrapping every small group in another surface.
recommendations: Use header, panel, and footer slots to separate task context, content, and completion actions.

boundaries: Shares are relative to the first stage, not to the previous one. State step conversion in text when it matters.
recommendations: Order stages as users move through them, and keep one hue: length already shows the drop-off.

boundaries: Use Table for data with row and column relationships. Visual columns do not establish table semantics.
recommendations: Group peer content and check reading order as columns change. Test long content at narrow widths.

boundaries: Use Fieldset for a form question and Toolbar for command keyboard behavior. Group only controls visual arrangement.
recommendations: Cluster compact controls that share a purpose and keep their labels clear.

boundaries: Visual size does not replace semantic level. Avoid skipping heading levels to obtain a particular appearance.
recommendations: Choose level from the document hierarchy and size from the desired visual emphasis.

boundaries: Color shows magnitude, not causation. Use a table when reading individual values is the primary task.
recommendations: Name both matrix dimensions and the value scale. Keep exact values available through the data table.

boundaries: Use Grid when columns need alignment across rows. Inline does not supply group or toolbar semantics.
recommendations: Use wrapping rows for related content that can remain understandable across multiple lines.

boundaries: The application decides what each claim cites. Inline Citation shows the source; it fetches only each site's favicon.
Streaming Text places citations for you. Use Inline Citation in your own text, such as Markdown or a summary.
recommendations: Put the chip right after the claim it supports. Give sources a title and a one-line description, so the preview says what the page backs up.

boundaries: Use Textarea for multiline text and Number Field for numeric stepping. Placeholder text is not a label.
recommendations: Use a visible label and the appropriate native type and autocomplete value. Keep examples in help text.
Input preserves native text editing and selection. Read-only values stay focusable; disabled values leave the tab order.
Pass defaultValue from a Server Component for an uncontrolled input. Keep value and onValueChange together in a Client Component for controlled editing.

boundaries: Keep the field label outside the input group. Decorative content must not replace the control's accessible name.
recommendations: Use prefixes and suffixes for units or context. Give embedded action buttons accessible names.

boundaries: Kbd describes keys. Shortcut registration, conflicts, and discoverability belong to the application.
recommendations: Show shortcuts that actually work and match the user's platform when the application supports it.

boundaries: Use Field Label inside Field compositions. Placeholder text and adjacent text do not replace label association.
recommendations: Associate htmlFor with the control's stable ID. Describe the expected value rather than an implementation detail.

boundaries: Use Dialog for editing tasks. Image loading and source quality remain application responsibilities.
recommendations: Give the image useful alternative text and a clear title. Keep the close action visible.

boundaries: Use Button for commands that do not navigate. Avoid vague labels such as Click here.
recommendations: Name the destination in the link text. Keep the real URL available for native browser navigation.
Use render for framework links. Put Next.js href or React Router to and routing options on that target. Do not nest anchors.

boundaries: Use Table for comparisons across columns. Avoid putting independent buttons inside a record-wide link.
recommendations: Give the list a name and keep record content separate from trailing actions.

boundaries: Mizen ships no parser. The app owns parsing, plugins, raw HTML policy, and URL sanitizing for untrusted content.
Footnote labels share one ID across documents on a page; this is a remark-rehype limitation.
recommendations: Render the document inside Markdown with markdownComponents, for example through react-markdown with remark-gfm and skipHtml.
Give each document an id and pass it as the parser's footnote prefix.

boundaries: Use link items for navigation. Forms and longer editing tasks belong in Popover or Dialog.
recommendations: Group related actions and keep destructive commands distinct. Use checkbox or radio items for persistent choices.

boundaries: Use Navigation Menu for site destinations. Menubar groups application commands with menu keyboard behavior.
recommendations: Use familiar command categories and consistent ordering. Keep individual menus short and task-focused.

boundaries: The application stores messages and runs turns. Message shows one turn; Edit only reports the new text.
Show time in the reader's time zone. Format it on the client or from their settings, and pass the instant as dateTime.
recommendations: Use from="user" for people and from="agent" for the agent's turn, and put AgentThinking, ToolCallGroup, and StreamingText inside the agent's Message in the order they arrive. Add author and avatar only in group chats.

boundaries: Use Progress for task completion. Meter represents a measurement within a known range.
recommendations: Label the measured quantity and its range. Show units and the exact value when they affect decisions.

boundaries: The component presents values. Calculations, rounding policy, and freshness belong to the application.
recommendations: Pair the value with its unit and reporting period. Explain the comparison or source in the description.

boundaries: The application supplies the trend visualization and calculations. Color alone must not indicate improvement.
recommendations: State the reporting period and the comparison baseline. Keep the current value readable without interpreting the plot.
Put the legend in actions and pass legend={false} to the chart. Set good="down" on MetricDelta for metrics where a fall is good, such as refunds.

boundaries: Use Menu for commands. Route matching and framework navigation remain application responsibilities.
recommendations: Use destination names and mark the current route. Keep menus short enough to scan without searching.

boundaries: Use Input for identifiers such as account numbers. Validate numeric business limits again on submission.
recommendations: Set meaningful bounds and steps. Specify locale and formatting when displaying currency or other units.

boundaries: Completing the slots does not verify the code. Expiry, rate limits, and verification belong to the server.
recommendations: State the code length and delivery method. Allow paste and show verification errors near the field.

boundaries: Do not hide essential actions behind a count. Use a full list when reviewing every item is the task.
visibleCount is fixed, not viewport-measured.
recommendations: Keep the most useful items visible and label the overflow action with what it reveals.

boundaries: The application owns fetching and page state. Use Data Table Pagination for a managed table instance.
recommendations: Keep page destinations shareable and mark the current page. Disable unavailable previous and next actions.

boundaries: Use non-negative parts from the same total. Use Category Comparison for signed or independent values.
recommendations: Name the whole and each part. Use a deliberate part order and keep the complete legend visible.

boundaries: Use Tooltip for brief noninteractive help. Use Dialog when the task needs modal focus.
recommendations: Keep the content tied to its trigger. Use a title when the popup presents a task or settings.

boundaries: Do not put required actions or instructions only in a hover preview. Use Popover for explicit interaction.
recommendations: Show supplementary context for a linked resource. Keep the destination understandable without the preview.

boundaries: Use Meter for bounded measurements. Do not invent percentages from elapsed time.
recommendations: Name the operation and use actual completion data. Use an indeterminate state when progress cannot be measured.

boundaries: Each ring measures progress toward its own goal. Do not compare ring lengths across rings with different goals.
recommendations: Use display strings for units such as "1h 45m". Keep to three rings so each stays distinct.

boundaries: Use Table for comparisons across multiple records. Property List describes one resource through label/value pairs.
recommendations: Use consistent property names and readable values. Order the most useful facts first.

boundaries: The application sends the answers back to the agent. Question Card collects them and reports them once, after the last question.
Ask only what the agent cannot decide itself. Use Approval Card to ask permission for one action.
recommendations: Keep each question to one decision with two to five options, put the trade-off in each option's description, and leave Something else on unless the options cover every case.

boundaries: Readers judge radar areas poorly. Use it for profiles on one shared scale, and CategoryComparison when exact differences matter.
Axis order changes the shape; keep it fixed across charts that readers compare.
recommendations: Normalize measures to one scale, such as 0–10, and state the scale in the label.

boundaries: Outer rings look longer than inner ones at the same value. Use RadialBars for a compact ranking; use BarList or CategoryComparison when readers compare values.
recommendations: Keep labels and exact values in the tiles, and fold small items into "Other".

boundaries: Use Checkbox Group when multiple choices are allowed. Use Select when a compact list better fits the task.
recommendations: Give the group one question and each option a distinct value. Use descriptions for meaningful differences.

boundaries: Two columns only: every link runs from a source to a target. Split multi-step flows into several charts.
recommendations: Order sources and targets so the largest flows run straight across; that keeps ribbons from crossing.

boundaries: Association does not establish causation. The application owns statistical analysis and data preparation.
recommendations: Label both axes and units. Give points meaningful names and preserve access to exact values.

boundaries: The score is the sum of part values; use it only when parts add up to a meaningful total.
recommendations: Name the score's meaning beside it, such as "Excellent", and keep part labels short.

boundaries: Use TableContainer for tables and CodeBlockContent for code. Avoid nested scrolling without a clear task reason.
recommendations: Keep scroll regions bounded and their content reachable by keyboard. Preserve visible context around wide content.
Constrain the parent height when content must scroll.

boundaries: Section provides arrangement. The caller supplies the heading and accessible document structure.
recommendations: Group one topic or task and give it a heading when it forms a document section.

boundaries: Use Tabs for switching panels and Radio Group for a longer form question.
recommendations: Use short labels for a small set of peer choices. Keep the selected value visible.

boundaries: Use Combobox for text filtering. Multiple selection needs visible selected values and a clear way to change them.
recommendations: Label the field and use readable option names. Provide explicit labels when values are objects.
SelectLabel names the trigger. Enter or Space opens the popup; arrow keys move through options and typing finds matching labels. Escape dismisses it.
Uncontrolled composition with serializable items can live in a Server Component. Controlled values, callbacks, and object formatting functions belong in a Client Component.

boundaries: Do not add a divider between every item. Use headings to explain the relationship between sections.
recommendations: Use a divider between meaningful groups when spacing alone does not separate them clearly.

boundaries: Use Dialog for short centered tasks. Avoid stacking sheets for a multi-step workflow.
recommendations: Keep the task related to the underlying page. Put the title and completion controls in predictable positions.

boundaries: Keep placeholders out of the accessibility reading order. Show an explicit error when loading fails.
recommendations: Match the expected content's broad shape and preserve layout space while loading.

boundaries: Use Number Field when exact entry matters more than relative adjustment. Sliders need meaningful bounds.
recommendations: Show the current value and units. Give each thumb a name when selecting a range.
Use getAriaLabel to name each thumb in a range.

boundaries: The application finds and stores sources. Sources shows them; it fetches only each site's favicon.
Show sources the agent used for this reply, not every search result it saw.
recommendations: Pass every source part as it arrives; Sources drops repeats. Give documents a title so they read as more than a domain.

boundaries: Use layout gaps for ordinary spacing. Spacer requires a flex layout with available space.
recommendations: Use available flex space to separate supporting controls from the main action.

boundaries: Use Button loading for button actions and Progress for measurable completion. A spinner does not announce the operation by itself.
recommendations: Place loading feedback beside the operation and explain what is pending.

boundaries: Use Section when a document region needs section semantics. Stack does not add accessible structure by itself.
recommendations: Arrange related content in reading order. Gaps follow the 4px scale: 1 for a title and its description, 6 between fields, 8 between groups; larger gaps between groups than inside them.

boundaries: The dot is a supporting indicator. Use visible text when the state affects a user's next action.
recommendations: Provide a label that names the status and keep it close to the affected resource.

boundaries: The application owns transitions and validation. A step indicator does not authorize skipping required steps.
recommendations: Name each step and show completed, current, and upcoming states. Explain how users can return to earlier work.

boundaries: The application owns the stream, retries, and where feedback is stored. Streaming Text shows them; it does not fetch or send anything.
It renders plain text with inline citations. Use Markdown for formatted replies.
recommendations: Pass the reply so far on every update and set status to complete when the stream ends. Place each citation right after the claim it supports.

boundaries: Use Checkbox for choices collected before submission. The application owns saving and rollback.
recommendations: Describe the setting in its enabled state. Keep immediate changes visible and explain failed updates.

boundaries: Table provides semantic presentation, not sorting or row-selection state.
Use Data Table when the task needs filtering, sorting, selection, or virtualization.
recommendations: Use row headers for identifying columns and align numeric values consistently.
Keep wide records inside the named TableContainer scroll region.

boundaries: Use navigation links for routes. Tabs change views within the current context.
recommendations: Use concise labels for related panels. Keep panel headings and reading order consistent.

boundaries: The application runs the agent and stores the plan. Task List shows each step's state; Approve, Revise, and Retry only report the choice.
Use it for steps the agent decides on before it starts. Calls it makes along the way belong in Tool Call Group.
recommendations: Keep step titles short and in the imperative, such as "Run the visual tests". Update each step's status as the agent works, and mark exactly one step as running.

boundaries: The application runs the command and streams its output. Terminal shows it; it never runs anything.
Output renders as text with red, bold, and dim kept. Other terminal colors show as plain text, and cursor moves are dropped.
recommendations: Pass the output as it grows and the exit code once it ends, so a failure opens on its own. Put a turn's commands next to its tool calls, in the order they ran.

boundaries: Use Heading for headings and Label for controls. Text renders body paragraphs.
recommendations: Use body for prose, ui for dense interface text, and caption for metadata. Set tone="muted" for supporting text; muted ink keeps readable contrast at every size.

boundaries: Use Input for single-line values. Textarea does not sanitize or interpret submitted content.
recommendations: Show the expected content and any length limit near the field. Allow enough space to review a normal response.

boundaries: Use Avatar for a person or identity. Image fetching and fallback policy remain application responsibilities.
recommendations: Choose a size that supports recognition. Describe informative images and use empty alt text for decorative ones.

boundaries: The value has no date or timezone. Resolve those explicitly before storing an instant.
recommendations: State which local time the field represents. Set native bounds and step where the task requires them.

boundaries: Do not turn missing data into zero. Aggregation intervals and timezone meaning belong to the application.
Put formatter callbacks in a Client Component. Data and timeZone remain caller-owned.
recommendations: Label the series and units. Choose the reporting timezone explicitly and preserve gaps for missing observations.

boundaries: Use date inputs for editable local values. A timestamp represents an instant, not an unresolved local appointment.
recommendations: Provide a timezone-bearing instant and choose locale and timezone explicitly for consistent output.

boundaries: Keep critical errors and required decisions on the page. Toasts are temporary feedback.
recommendations: Mount ToastProvider once at the app boundary. Add AnchoredToastProvider for anchored feedback. Examples use their shared managers.
Report the outcome of an action in a short message. Offer a relevant recovery action when available.

boundaries: Use Button for a one-time action. Use Switch for an immediate setting with explicit on/off meaning.
recommendations: Name the option being enabled. Keep its label stable between pressed and unpressed states.

boundaries: Use Segmented Control for a single choice. Use Toolbar when the group also contains unrelated commands.
recommendations: Group related formatting or selection options. Name icon-only toggles and make selected states visible.

boundaries: Use Token for metadata, filters, and reversible selections. Combobox owns multi-select input behavior.
recommendations: Use a short label, two or three meaningful category colors, and icons only when they help recognition. Keep hidden labels accessible.

boundaries: The application runs tools and stores approvals. Tool Call shows each call's state; Approve and Deny only report the choice.
Arguments and results render as given. Remove secrets before passing them in.
recommendations: Map each SDK tool part to one call with its toolCallId, and group a turn's calls with ToolCallGroup. Write the title in present tense while running and past tense when complete.

boundaries: Use Button Group when independent Tab stops are preferable. The toolbar does not execute application commands.
recommendations: Group commands by purpose and label icon-only controls. Keep keyboard order aligned with visual order.
Name the toolbar and use its arrow-key navigation to move between controls.

boundaries: Do not place interactive content in a tooltip; use Popover.
Keep required instructions visible rather than available only on hover.
recommendations: Use a short explanation for a control whose intent needs clarification.
Group adjacent hints with TooltipProvider. Use TooltipCreateHandle for one popup that moves between detached triggers.

boundaries: Use Side Navigation for grouped route links. The application owns resource loading and activation outcomes.
recommendations: Use resource names and stable identifiers. Keep expansion distinct from selection and activation.

boundaries: Do not hide instructions needed by sighted users. Keep interactive controls visibly reachable.
recommendations: Use hidden text to clarify an otherwise ambiguous control or visual indicator.

boundaries: Suggestion sends nothing itself. onClick receives the prompt, and the application sends it.
Keep each prompt short enough to read at a glance; long prompts make the row scroll.
recommendations: Show a few starters above an empty composer, and send the label as the message as is. Disable the row while the agent works.

boundaries: The application sends messages and streams replies. Conversation lays out and scrolls the thread; it stores nothing.
Give it a parent with a bounded height, such as a full-height panel. It does not size the page.
recommendations: Key each turn by its message id and pass the person's turns as Message from="user", so they settle near the top when sent. Set busy while a reply streams, and add navigation once threads get long.

boundaries: Message Scroller handles scrolling only: it renders no messages and fetches no history.
Keep messageId stable across renders; an index shifts when earlier messages load and breaks the reader's place.
recommendations: Use Conversation for an agent thread; reach for Message Scroller for other transcripts, such as a team chat or a log. Anchor turns the person sends, and load earlier messages above without scrolling yourself.
